title: Work Item state machine and recovery
outOfScope: Provider API mutation or real external identity/approval behavior
Changing release publication, installation, or upgrade semantics

sources.reason: Canonical Work Item lifecycle commands and closure order.
Existing start transition and receipt behavior.
Existing finish and archive transition behavior.
Archived lifecycle evidence index and digest conventions.
Existing lifecycle state vocabulary and recovery boundary.

rawUserRequest: Execute all Work Items serially with the complete Contract, implementation, verification, PR, merge, archive, close, branch cleanup, and base synchronization workflow; record and correct process issues before continuing. Japanese capability is mandatory before publishing.

rawRequestSource.reference: user-request: AI Cockpit comprehensive remediation instruction and continuation authorization

riskAssessment.reason: State transitions, evidence binding, recovery, idempotency, and local/remote lifecycle consistency can otherwise allow closure or completion claims to bypass required gates.

executionDecision.reason: User authorized serial execution and the WI-07 boundary is deterministic and local.

preReviewWarnings: Review fail-closed transitions and recovery evidence before claiming closure.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A deterministic state machine models the canonical, paused, blocked, cancelled, rollback, and stale states with transition preconditions, evidence fields, event identity, role, recoverability, and reversibility.

Invalid ordering, stale base, Contract/Summary mismatch, digest mismatch, wrong branch/PR/merge, unauthorized cleanup, provider partial success, and rollback state each return a blocked result with a resume condition.
Repeated start, finish, archive, and close events use stable event identity and do not duplicate archive or event records.
Interrupted archive, branch creation failure, close network failure, CI delay, and local/remote mismatch produce recoverable non-closed states.
Focused checks, full project checks, and the complete PR/merge/archive/close/cleanup/base-sync lifecycle pass without external mutation.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.

intent.problem: The repository has lifecycle commands and evidence artifacts, but the allowed transition graph and recovery/idempotency rules are distributed across scripts and documents. This makes illegal ordering, interrupted operations, and local/remote divergence harder to detect mechanically.
constraints: Keep the state evaluator deterministic and offline.
Preserve existing lifecycle commands and archived evidence compatibility.
Fail closed on missing, stale, contradictory, or provider-unconfirmed evidence.
Do not claim provider identity, enterprise approval, or production readiness from local fixtures.
intent.rationale: A single executable transition model plus negative recovery corpus makes lifecycle closure auditable without changing external provider behavior.

declaredIntent.summary: Enforce a deterministic local Work Item state machine and recovery boundary without changing external provider behavior.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Canonical lifecycle transitions accept only the documented order.
Illegal order, stale base, mismatched evidence, and wrong merge fail closed.
Retries, interruption, partial provider state, and duplicate events remain safe and idempotent.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: User explicitly authorized serial execution and lifecycle evidence updates within the Work Item Contract scope.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff and restore related tests and docs.
